paper.title: EXG: Self-Evolving Agents with Experience Graphs
paper.central_claim: EXG organizes accumulated successes and failures into a typed experience graph (case nodes, task anchors, similar_to and fixed_by edges) that supports online cross-task reuse and offline reuse as a frozen external memory and plugs into existing self-evolving agents; across code generation and multi-hop QA benchmarks it attains better pass@1/pass@2 with fewer LLM calls (up to 45.7%) and lower latency (up to 30.5%) than reflection- and memory-based baselines.

evidence.quote: we introduce EXG, an experience graph framework for self-evolving agents that explicitly organizes accumulated successes and failures into a structured, relational representation
evidence.support_explanation: Central object: cross-task experience graph (case nodes, task anchors, similar_to/fixed_by edges) used as external memory injected as hints.

evidence.quote: indicates whether the attempt is successful
evidence.support_explanation: Case outcome r in {0,1} (golden vs warning) comes from a correctness signal (unit tests / gold answers) that the stream provides after every attempt.

evidence.quote: Correction edges. For multiple attempts on the same task
evidence.support_explanation: fixed_by edges link a failed attempt to the later corrected attempt on the SAME task (requires a retry within the task).

evidence.quote: The final retrieval pool aggregates diverse and complementary signals by combining anchor cases from the current task, semantically similar cases retrieved via seed-based expansion, and associated corrective evidence
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval = task anchor + similarity expansion + fixed_by traces, deduplicated and capped.

evidence.quote: is used solely to order cases for selection and does not modify the experience graph
evidence.support_explanation: Relevance scores never feed back into the graph: no utility credit, demotion, or retirement.

evidence.quote: Fixed-by hints are added with the highest priority, followed by warning hints and golden hints.
evidence.support_explanation: Hint budget H=5 allocated by type priority.

evidence.quote: The finalized case is then incorporated back into the experience graph according to the graph update rules.
evidence.support_explanation: Every attempt (success or failure) is appended; the loop is online across tasks.

evidence.quote: During evaluation, newly generated cases are not added to the graph, and no new similarity or corrective edges are created.
evidence.support_explanation: Offline setting freezes the graph and avoids test-task leakage; online setting does not.

evidence.quote: Each task is allowed up to two attempts, consisting of a single initial attempt followed by at most one retry.
evidence.support_explanation: pass@1 / pass@2 protocol; retry after failure uses correctness feedback.

evidence.quote: Effectiveness is evaluated using pass@1 and pass@2, while efficiency is measured by the avarage number of LLM calls, LLM inference latency, and retrieval latency.
evidence.support_explanation: Metrics; no repeated runs, seeds, or intervals mentioned anywhere in main text or appendices.

evidence.quote: the dataset is randomly shuffled and split into a 7:3 ratio for online collection and offline evaluation, respectively
evidence.support_explanation: Offline holdout: single random 70/30 split per benchmark; no near-duplicate or contamination audit.

evidence.quote: on HumanEval with Qwen3-1.7B, EXG improves pass@1 by more than 150% relative to Reflexion
evidence.support_explanation: Headline relative gain over a very low baseline (Reflexion pass@1 about 0.2); Reflexion and SE-Agent keep no cross-task memory.

evidence.quote_unavailable_reason: Table 1 cells are interleaved/duplicated in the HTML extraction (rows hold ~26 numbers for 14 columns); cell-level values cannot be audited, only prose-reported figures are used.
evidence.support_explanation: Reflexion pass@1 on HumanEval appears as ~0.20 for Qwen3-1.7B/8B while EXG variants reach 0.5-0.8; baseline strength and harness quality cannot be verified from the pinned text.

evidence.quote: On HumanEval, the base EXG method requires 1.20 calls per task, compared to 1.83 for Reflexion and 2.21 for SE-Agent, corresponding to reductions of 34.4% and 45.7% , respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Efficiency claim: fewer LLM calls mainly because plain EXG has no reflection step and succeeds more often on the first attempt.

evidence.quote: the retrieval overhead introduced by the experience graph is minimal
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval ~18-22 ms; graph construction/similarity-edge computation cost not reported.

evidence.quote: slightly below ExpeL’s 0.909
evidence.support_explanation: Offline HumanEval test pass@1: EXG-Reflexion 0.879 vs ExpeL 0.909 (reported as negative/comparable).

evidence.quote: In the offline test stage, EXG-Reflexion continues to outperform ExpeL, achieving pass@1 of 0.610 and pass@2 of 0.637 , compared to 0.590 and 0.633 , respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Offline HotpotQA: +0.020 / +0.004 over ExpeL, single split, no intervals.

evidence.quote: removing correction edges leads to the largest performance drop, indicating that explicit corrective information from failures to successful solutions provides a stable and significant benefit
evidence.support_explanation: Structural ablation claim (Figure 6, values not given in text).

evidence.quote: On HumanEval, the number of fixed_by edges remains consistently low, ranging from around 3 to 10, corresponding to roughly 3–11% of cases participating in explicit correction relations.
evidence.support_explanation: Core EXG HumanEval graph averages 3.6 fixed_by edges per ~100 cases; this sits uneasily with 'removing correction edges gives the largest drop'.

evidence.quote: Table 3. Hint type ablation study of EXG on HumanEval. Group pass@1 pass@2 No-Memory 0.610 0.640 Similar-Only 0.823 0.835 Warning-Only 0.866 0.884 EXG 0.872 0.896
evidence.support_explanation: Memory-off 0.610 -> flat similar golden cases 0.823 -> +warning 0.866 -> full 0.872: most of the gain comes from retrieving similar golden cases; graph-specific increments are +0.049 / +0.006 p@1; no intervals; model not stated.

evidence.quote: Similar-Only injects only golden cases retrieved by similarity, providing correct but limited guidance.
evidence.support_explanation: Similar-Only is effectively the nearest-neighbour memory baseline.

evidence.quote: By the end of the task sequence, EXG-based methods attain a cumulative Pass@1 of approximately 80%, while baseline methods plateau near 55–58%.
evidence.support_explanation: Learning curve over the HumanEval stream; the rising trend supports retained, compounding benefit of the store.

evidence.quote: Reflexion consumes 117,378 total tokens across all tasks, whereas EXG consumes 125,304 tokens, corresponding to a modest increase of 6.8% in total token usage.
evidence.support_explanation: Token cost disclosed: total tokens up 6.8% on HumanEval, down 20.4% on MuSiQue.

evidence.quote: Accordingly, approaches that aim to explicitly model experience-driven agent evolution do not fall within the scope of memory systems
evidence.support_explanation: Authors scope away agent-memory systems (cross-task memory neighbours) rather than comparing to them.

evidence.quote: Online self-evolving methods typically confine experience to a single task, lacking mechanisms to persist and reuse experience across tasks during inference.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap; the online baselines (Reflexion, SE-Agent) were chosen as per-task methods.

evidence.quote: EXG is the first experience graph designed for self-evolving agents
evidence.support_explanation: Novelty claim by assertion.

evidence.quote: All models used in this work are accessed exclusively through APIs
evidence.support_explanation: Models served via API (Qwen3 sizes, Qwen-Plus/Max); no pretraining contamination analysis for HumanEval/EvalPlus/HotpotQA/MuSiQue.

evidence.quote: evaluate whether explicitly structuring experience as a graph can complement existing online self-evolution mechanisms without increasing the number of model calls or modifying the underlying agent logic
evidence.support_explanation: Plug-and-play variants EXG-Reflexion / EXG-SE / EXG-SE-Rev.

evidence.quote: This confirms that graph growth is approximately linear in the number of tasks rather than in the number of attempts
evidence.support_explanation: Append-only growth; no consolidation, size bound, or retirement.

evidence.quote: ensuring that observed improvements reflect genuine semantic correctness rather than overfitting to limited tests
evidence.support_explanation: EvalPlus used as stricter check on the same HumanEval problems (not an independent set).

evidence.quote: This gap can be partially attributed to the reduced volume of reflection traces collected online by EXG-Reflexion
evidence.support_explanation: Author explanation of offline HumanEval shortfall; untested.

evidence.quote: are treated as golden cases
evidence.support_explanation: Successful attempts stored as golden cases containing the produced output (code/answer) of the earlier task; hints reuse them as exemplars.

signatures.object: Cross-task experience store: from per-task Reflexion/SE-Agent state (no persistence across tasks) to a growing graph of attempt-level cases injected as hints before each attempt.
signatures.information: Task input, produced output, success bit from tests/gold answers, extracted execution signature (errors, failure type); correctness signal is available after each attempt (oracle labels in the stream).
signatures.operation: Abstract each attempt into a case; add node + contain edge + similar_to edges (embedding similarity) + fixed_by edge when a retry fixes an earlier failure; retrieve task-anchor, similarity-neighbourhood and fixed_by cases; rerank by prompt+failure similarity with one-hop propagation; assemble <=5 hints by priority (fixed-by > warning > golden).
signatures.output: Hint block in the prompt; updated graph after each attempt.
signatures.conditions: Short-horizon tasks (<=2 attempts) with machine-checkable correctness; related tasks recur; K_s=10, F_sim=5, K_c=30, alpha=0.8, H=5.
signatures.feedback: Binary correctness per attempt (+ error signature).
signatures.selection_rule: No admission or retirement gate: every attempt is appended; selection is only at retrieval/rerank time.
signatures.selection_data: Same stream being evaluated (online, prequential) or 70% collection split (offline).
signatures.persistence: Graph store in memory/FAISS index; offline graph frozen; no pruning.
signatures.later_use: Next tasks' first and retry attempts (hints).
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher pass@1/pass@2, up to 45.7% fewer LLM calls, up to 30.5% lower inference latency; offline comparable to ExpeL.
signatures.failure_boundary: Needs outcome labels at deployment; benefits scale with task regularity; HotpotQA gains smaller; offline HumanEval below ExpeL.

gap.author_gap: Online self-evolving methods keep experience task-local; offline methods need heavy post-processing; no unified, structured experience organization bridges online cross-task reuse and offline memory.
gap.checked_gap: Cross-task persistence is a real limitation of Reflexion/SE-Agent, but those baselines are per-task by design, so the headline comparisons mainly measure 'cross-task memory vs none'. Directly relevant cross-task memory neighbours (online memory/cheatsheet/workflow-memory and graph-memory systems) are scoped out in related work rather than compared; only ExpeL is run (offline).
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Reflexion (Shinn 2023) -> SE-Agent (Lin 2025) per-task; ExpeL (Zhao 2024) offline insight extraction; agent memory systems (Zheng 2024, Wang 2024, etc.) dismissed as out of scope. Versions as cited; no neighbour full texts in this pack.
gap.residue: Whether graph structure adds value beyond flat similar-case retrieval; maintenance as the store grows.
gap.stakes: Repeated mistakes and growing inference cost in deployed agents.
gap.method_response: Typed relational store with correction edges and priority hint assembly.
gap.remaining_gap: Retirement/consolidation, labels-free deployment, statistically reliable comparison with flat memory.
unresolved: Closest cross-task memory neighbours are not available as pinned text and are not run as baselines.
